sentences.text: Mioaetus is an extinct genus of accipitrids, a family of birds of prey, meaning "Miocene eagle".
The species was described by Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme from fossils found in the Hammerschmiede clay pit in Germany.
The only known species in this genus is M. pforzenensis, which serves as the type species.
Mioaetus is currently considered a valid taxon classified as a member of the family Accipitridae.
Mioaetus lived during the Miocene epoch, specifically in the early Late Miocene (earliest Tortonian) of southern Germany.
The environment at the Hammerschmiede site supported a productive river system that likely provided ample prey for piscivorous birds like Mioaetus.
